hints: Number density $n$ means number of free electrons per unit volume, so calculate the volume of the cylindrical wire using $V = A \times L$ first.
teacher_walkthrough: Number density is defined as total number of carriers per unit volume: $$n = \frac{N}{V}$$ where volume of uniform wire is $$V = AL$$
common_pitfalls: Dividing by area or length alone instead of by the full volume $AL$, giving incorrect power of 10.
For a show that question, omitting clear substitution and volume step so the proof is not credited.
Writing unit as $\text{m}^3$ instead of $\text{m}^{-3}$ for a per unit volume quantity.

hints: Current is rate of flow of charge $I = Q/t$. Convert the time to SI units before dividing.
Drift speed links current to carrier density by $I = nAvq$, where $q$ is the elementary charge $1.6 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$ and $n$ is the value from (a).
Rearrange to $v = I/(nAq)$ and check powers of 10 carefully when multiplying $n \times A \times q$.
teacher_walkthrough: Current is defined by $$I = \frac{Q}{t}$$ with $t$ in seconds.
Drift current relation is $$I = nAvq$$ where $q = e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$. Rearranged: $$v = \frac{I}{nAq}$$
$$v = \frac{1.147}{2.04 \times 10^{4}} = 5.6 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$$ in the direction of conventional current opposite to electron flow.
common_pitfalls: Leaving time as 2.5 minutes instead of 150 s, which overestimates current by a factor of 60.
Omitting the electron charge $1.6 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$ or using total number $N$ instead of number density $n$ in $I = nAvq$.
Power of 10 errors when combining $10^{28} \times 10^{-6} \times 10^{-19}$, often giving $10^{-4}$ instead of $10^{-5}$ for $v$.
